The Benue Strategic Alliance for Tinubu/Shettima 2027 has vowed to mobilise support exclusively for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election, insisting that its political disagreement with Governor Hyacinth Alia’s camp will not affect its commitment to the President’s second-term ambition. The Director-General of the alliance, Akange Audu, stated this in a statement made available to journalists in Makurdi on Saturday, titled, ‘Benue APC crisis: Stop the political blackmail, allow us to work for Tinubu’. He was reacting to comments by the Director-General of the Tinubu/Alia Re-election Campaign, Richard Asema, who, during a press conference in Makurdi on Friday, rejected the alliance and alleged that its activities could frustrate Alia’s re-election. Rejecting the allegation, Audu said the alliance was not an enemy of Tinubu, explaining that it provided a political platform for aggrieved APC members and stakeholders from other political parties who shared the President’s re-election ambition. Audu said the alliance was established to mobilise support for Tinubu ahead of the 2027 general elections and was not formed to challenge the governor or take over the leadership of the All Progressives Congress in the state. Tinubu pledges to rebuild violence-ravaged Plateau communities 2027: Atiku, Makinde near alliance deal Tinubu, Aregbesola met three times despite rift – APC chieftain, Prof Adeyeye Audu maintained that the group was not seeking to reclaim political positions within the APC but wanted to provide its members with a platform to organise and support Tinubu’s second-term ambition. He argued that the President’s re-election should be treated as a broader national political project that could accommodate different political interests, irrespective of their relationship with the Benue State governor. “The Alliance believes that President Tinubu’s re-election should be treated as a broader national political project capable of accommodating diverse political interests, including individuals and groups who may not share Governor Alia’s political preferences,” he said. The alliance leader further claimed that its membership included elected APC executive council members at the state, local government and ward levels, whose structures were allegedly dissolved by the governor. He also listed the three senators representing Benue State, 10 members of the House of Representatives and several members of the state House of Assembly among its supporters. Audu added that the group had the backing of political stakeholders and opinion leaders who played significant roles in Alia’s emergence as governor in the 2023 elections. He said many of them remained loyal to the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Senator George Akume, whom he described as the leader of Benue politics. “These are individuals who, despite their loyalty to the APC, have remained committed supporters of Sen. Dr George Akume, CON, Secretary to the Government of the Federation and Leader of Benue Politics, and continue to enjoy his political goodwill and support across the state,” the statement added. John Charles
